title: Run the daemon as its own restricted user, not as the login user
description:
`nixadmin-daemon` is a systemd **user** service (`nix/module.nix:320`), so it runs
as the login user with that account's full authority: the whole home directory —
SSH keys, browser profiles, credentials, documents — plus the session bus. The
process running an LLM and reacting to system events is the same principal that
owns everything the person cares about.

Give it a dedicated system user with only what it needs.

## Why this is worth doing

**Blast radius.** Nothing about the daemon's job requires read access to
`~/.ssh` or a browser profile. Today a bug or a prompt-injected tool call is
bounded only by what the human user can do.

**It closes the residual we document publicly.** `users.users.${cfg.user}.extraGroups
= [ "nixadmin" ]` (`module.nix:288`) puts the *login user* in the group that owns
the `root:nixadmin 0660` helper socket. So anything running as that user can talk
to the helper directly and skip `SafetyGate` — the confirm and the
test-before-switch invariant live in the daemon, not in the helper. If only the
daemon's own user is in that group, that bypass closes and the gate becomes a
real boundary rather than a convention.

**It unlocks systemd hardening**, which a user service largely cannot use:
`ProtectHome=`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `PrivateTmp=`, `NoNewPrivileges=`,
`RestrictAddressFamilies=`, `SystemCallFilter=`, plus `StateDirectory=` and
`RuntimeDirectory=` instead of XDG paths.

## What makes it non-trivial

Not a `User=` line — the split is architectural. Known obstacles:

1. **The tray and web clients must stay user services.** Both need the session
   bus and the desktop's SNI tray host (`module.nix:336`, `:353`). They already
   talk to the daemon over a socket, so the shape is: daemon becomes a system
   service, clients stay per-user and connect across the user boundary. The
   daemon's client socket then needs a group the humans are in — note this is a
   *different* group from the helper socket's, and conflating them would re-open
   exactly the bypass this change is meant to close.

2. **The flake directory is the crux.** The action tier makes deterministic
   writes to `cfg.flakeDir`, which is owned by the login user. A separate daemon
   user needs write access there — but if the daemon user can write the flake
   that root then activates, some of the isolation is given straight back. Worth
   deciding explicitly: group-writable checkout, a daemon-owned worktree that the
   human merges, or the daemon proposing a patch it cannot itself apply. This
   decision probably deserves its own ADR.

3. **D-Bus monitors use both buses.** `monitors.py:81` selects
   `BusType.SYSTEM` or `SESSION` per monitor. System-bus monitors are fine under
   a system user; session-bus ones break, since there is no session. Either drop
   them, proxy them through a user-side client, or keep a thin user-side monitor
   that forwards events to the daemon.

4. **Rootless Ollama.** `nixadmin-ollama` is a user service using rootless
   Podman, and `render`/`video` are granted to the login user
   (`module.nix:288-289`). Simplest path: leave Ollama with the human user — the
   daemon reaches it over `127.0.0.1`, so no group changes are needed. Moving it
   to the daemon user would need subuid/subgid and lingering for that account.

5. **Journal access.** Reading logs needs the `systemd-journal` group, currently
   free because the daemon runs as a human who has it.

6. **Lingering becomes unnecessary** for the daemon. The tmpfiles linger rule
   (`module.nix:296`) exists so user services start without an interactive login;
   a system service does not need it. The tray and web clients still do.

## Acceptance

- `nixadmin-daemon` runs as a dedicated `isSystemUser` with no shell and no home
- the login user is no longer in the helper-socket group
- clients reach the daemon over a socket whose group is distinct from the helper's
- systemd hardening directives applied and the service still passes
  `systemd-analyze security nixadmin-daemon`
- the flake-directory write path is a documented decision, not an accident

title: Autofix engine: act on unit-failure events
description: Connect systemd unit-failure events (already subscribed via monitors -> services JobRemoved) to the remediation tier using the act/ask matrix: safe+reversible -> auto-remediate with undo-after; else the one rare push. Plumbing exists; policy does not. See docs/ux.md.
notes: 2026-07-26: BUILT on feat/autofix. autofix.py pure policy (decide) + daemon engine (_run_autofix/_autofix_unit) triggered by the services JobRemoved event. Restart+verify via remediation tier (both scopes; system via root helper, configurable). Restart-loop guard reads autofix history from the event store; past maxAttempts -> inform. Episode dedup + startup seeding. Delivery via Event + Timeline; desktop notifications/offers deferred to b43 (2b). Tests: test_autofix_smoke + 3 server tests.

title: Unify web operations and humanize activity
description:
The web hub still presents work differently depending on where it starts and exposes internal event kinds in the primary Activity view. Make the presentation consistent and human-facing while preserving complete debugging evidence.

## Scope
- Use the operation-card presentation for invoke requests and actions initiated from failed-unit controls.
- Give restart, explain, and journal work clear running/success/failure states.
- Translate internal timeline kinds into concise human summaries.
- Group related service lifecycle events where a failure, attempted remediation, and recovery form one understandable episode.
- Keep raw event kinds, metadata, timestamps, statuses, and technical output under Details.
- Do not duplicate the human-facing answer inside Details.
acceptance_criteria: Restart/explain/journal controls use consistent operation feedback; Activity does not show raw snake_case kinds as its main label; adjacent related service events are grouped without hiding failures or outcomes; Details retains raw diagnostic evidence but does not duplicate the answer; five-item cursor pagination remains stable; focused tests and the full flake check pass.
close_reason: Unified invoke and failed-unit work in shared operation cards; added explicit restart/explain success semantics; humanized and grouped service activity; kept raw evidence under non-duplicating Details; 209 tests, full flake check, and headless Chromium smoke pass.

title: Add desktop launcher to restore the nixadmin tray
description:
Quitting the tray currently leaves no graphical way to bring it back; the user must run a command or restart the user unit. Add an application launcher that restores the systemd-managed tray instance and make the Quit action's scope clear.

## Scope
- Install a discoverable desktop application entry for nixadmin.
- Launching it should start or restart the systemd user tray service without creating an unmanaged duplicate process.
- Clarify in the tray UI that Quit exits only the tray client, not the daemon/helper/web services.
- Document and test the lifecycle behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A nixadmin entry appears in a desktop application launcher; activating it makes the tray icon available again through the systemd user service; repeated activation does not create duplicate tray processes; the tray Quit label or adjacent copy makes clear that only the tray is closed; daemon and other services remain running; Nix evaluation and relevant tests pass.
close_reason: Added a Nix-installed desktop launcher that idempotently restores the systemd-managed tray service; clarified the tray close action leaves nixadmin services running; added lifecycle assertion; full flake check and generated desktop entry build pass.

title: Simplify web hub timeline and change progress presentation
description:
The web hub is functionally strong but visually busy. Tighten the presentation while preserving diagnostic depth.

## Scope
- Show only the 10 most recent timeline events initially.
- Add pagination so older events remain accessible without making the page indefinitely long.
- Present change operations in plain-language summary form by default.
- Move technical/debugging output into a collapsed Details disclosure, similar to the expandable thinking/tool areas in agent harnesses.
- While a change is running, show a clear Working on it progress state rather than leaving raw technical output as the primary feedback.
- Preserve cancellation, confirmation, failure reporting, and post-change verification.

## Design intent
Keep the hub calm and legible for non-technical users while retaining full evidence for debugging. Progressive disclosure should hide complexity, not remove it. Pagination must be backed by stable event ordering so events are neither duplicated nor skipped as new events arrive.
design: Prefer cursor-based pagination using the event sequence/id over offset pagination because the timeline can receive new events while a user views older pages. Use native HTML details/summary for accessible progressive disclosure unless interaction requirements prove it insufficient. Model operation presentation as explicit states (queued/running/awaiting confirmation/verifying/succeeded/failed/cancelled), with indeterminate progress until the backend exposes measurable phases.
acceptance_criteria: The initial timeline renders at most 10 events; users can navigate to older/newer pages; pagination remains stable if new events arrive; change cards show a concise human-readable state and progress indication; technical command/build/tool output is collapsed under an accessible Details control by default; errors remain prominent and actionable; existing cancel/confirm/timeline behavior remains covered by tests.
notes:
Additional presentation ideas after code review:
- Group related low-level events into one operation row where correlation metadata allows it (requested → testing → applying → verified), rather than making every internal event equally prominent.
- Use explicit user-facing phases: Preparing, Waiting for approval, Applying, Verifying, Complete. Keep raw daemon status and output inside Details.
- When viewing an older page, do not auto-jump to page one during the 20-second refresh; show a New activity button/badge instead.
- Use compact relative timestamps in the row with exact timestamp in title/details.
- Keep failures expanded or visually prominent even when routine technical details default closed.
- Consider Previous/Next labels rather than page numbers because cursor pagination does not have a cheap stable total-page count.

Current implementation fetches 100 rows in page.py and the protocol accepts only limit/unit. Cursor pagination therefore needs coordinated changes to store query, wire protocol, daemon handler, web client/API, and page rendering.
close_reason: Extracted the web hub into packaged HTML/CSS/ES modules; added stable 10-event cursor pagination, older/newer navigation and new-activity handling; added explicit operation progress phases and collapsed diagnostic details; expanded protocol/store/web tests. Full nix flake check passes.

title: Spotlight-style invoke overlay (the hub's shape, not a tab)
description:
The web hub is now a single pane of glass — prompt first, common-action chips,
task cards, machine status below (built 2026-08-13). It proves the interaction,
but a browser tab is the wrong container for it.

"Invoke, not resident" means summoned, used, and gone. A page you navigate to and
leave open is resident by construction: it sits in a tab accruing attention, which
is exactly what design-for-silence rejects. Spotlight is the right shape — a
keystroke anywhere, a prompt, an answer, gone.

## What this is asking for

A global hotkey that raises a small centred overlay with the same interaction the
hub now has (prompt · chips · reply card), dismissed on Escape or on completion.
No window in the taskbar, no state to return to.

## Open decisions

1. **Wrapper vs native.** Cheapest is to wrap the existing page — a borderless
   always-on-top webview pointed at `127.0.0.1:7677` with the chrome hidden, so
   the interaction stays HTML/JS and iterates fast. Native (libcosmic, ADR 0002 /
   `nix-nixadmin-7v2`) gets real overlay behaviour and no browser engine in the
   dependency tree. The wrapper is probably right *first*, precisely because the
   interaction is still moving.
2. **The hotkey under Wayland.** COSMIC has no global-hotkey protocol a client can
   grab unilaterally; the realistic path is a compositor shortcut bound in the
   COSMIC config that runs `nixadmin-invoke`, which is declarative config — a fit
   for nixlap, not something the daemon can do for itself.
3. **What the overlay does with the hub's other content.** Status, timeline and
   the kept-well ledger have no place in a spotlight. Likely split: the overlay is
   invoke-only, and the hub page remains the place you *look at* the machine — so
   the two surfaces diverge rather than one replacing the other.
4. **Whether a second surface is warranted at all** before the native-folding
   direction (`nix-nixadmin-edx`) is settled. An overlay is still a place to go,
   just a cheaper one; folding into the wifi icon and the app that won't open
   remains the moat.

## Not in scope

Voice as the primary invoke (`nix-nixadmin-4lo`) — same surface question, separate
decision.
notes: Implementation sequence agreed 2026-08-23: first extract the web hub into structured static modules and simplify timeline/change presentation in nix-nixadmin-si0. Then build a persistent GTK/WebKitGTK overlay spike that reuses the web components and measures summon-to-visible latency, focus behaviour, Escape dismissal, and operation persistence on COSMIC/Wayland. Keep the overlay compact; full history remains in the hub.

title: README: lead with the vision, and state that the agent is not given root
description:
The README opens with the vision as a blockquote and then drops straight into
the architecture diagram. Two problems for a cold reader — including anyone
evaluating the project rather than using it.

## 1. The vision does not carry far enough

`docs/vision.md` is the strongest writing in the repo: it separates the durable
asset from the implementation detail ("NixOS and the LLM are implementation
details"), and gives a prioritisation test someone else could apply — *does this
make the person think less in machine terms?* Right now the README quotes two
lines of it and moves on to `clients → daemon → modules`.

Lead with the thesis and let it breathe before the plumbing. The architecture
block is for people who already decided to care.

## 2. The security posture is buried, and it is the differentiator

Today the entire claim is one cell in an ASCII diagram:

    safety gate    privileged actions gated in code, not in prompts

That single line is the most distinguishing property of the project and most
readers will not register it. The default assumption on seeing "AI agent for
NixOS" is *someone gave a model root on their laptop*. State plainly that this is
the opposite of that.

What is actually true, and worth saying explicitly:

- **The model never gets a shell.** The privileged surface is a fixed enum —
  `test` / `switch` / `boot` / `revert`, plus a `restart` for a unit name
  validated against a charset-and-suffix allowlist. `ALLOWED_ACTIONS` in
  `nix/nixadmin-helper.py`.
- **The daemon holds no privilege.** It runs as a user service. Root work goes
  to a separate helper over a Unix socket, so the process reasoning about the
  system is never the process changing it.
- **`switch` needs a human and a passing test.** `safety.py` refuses it unless a
  `test` succeeded earlier in the same session *and* the user confirms — and it
  gates on the helper's real exit code, never on whether "failed" appears in the
  build output.
- **No shell anywhere.** argv is built from a template; nothing is interpolated
  into a command string.

The framing to land: this is a **predictable framework for common tasks**, not an
LLM one-shotting a root shell. Determinism where it matters, with the model
classifying, routing and explaining rather than authoring privileged actions.
The safety properties hold whether the model is having a good day or not, which
is the entire point of putting them in code instead of a prompt.

## Do not overclaim

State the residual honestly, or the section reads as marketing:

The helper socket is `root:nixadmin` `0660` and the login user is in that group,
so anything already running as that user can talk to the socket directly and skip
the daemon's confirm gate — still limited to those four actions against a fixed
flake dir, which the request cannot redirect. That is a property of the socket's
group permission, not something the agent is granted. Naming it costs nothing and
makes the rest credible.

## Related

- Depends on the outcome of nix-nixadmin-30y (naming) if the README is being
  rewritten anyway — decided since: **numen**, with `nixlap` keeping its name.
- The same correction is needed in nixlap's README, whose "Security model"
  section currently says an LLM agent "can reach root", conflating what the
  account can do with what the agent is given.
acceptance_criteria: README leads with the vision before the architecture diagram; a named section states the agent gets no shell and no root, backed by the fixed action enum, the unprivileged daemon, and the confirm+prior-test gate; the socket-group residual is stated rather than omitted.

title: Update checker + apply from the tray
description:
Detect that flake inputs have moved and offer to apply the update from the tray, replacing the nixlap nightly autoUpgrade that was just deleted.

## Context
nixlap removed system.autoUpgrade (2026-08-02). Two reasons: with upgrade=false it never touched flake.lock, so it could not pull a security patch — it only re-applied local edits, and on most nights rebuilt to the store path that was already current. And it handed an unattended root job a build of a user-writable directory, so anything able to write there (bad postinstall, browser exploit, or the agents that edit that repo by design) got root on a timer. This issue restores the genuinely useful half — actual input updates — with a human in the loop.
design:
Two halves, split along the existing privilege boundary.

1. Detector — a poll module in monitors.py. 'nix flake update' has no dry-run, so compare each locked rev in flake.lock against the remote ref (git ls-remote, or nix flake metadata --refresh) and fire when they diverge. Reuse the existing interval/trigger plumbing and concurrency cap.

2. Apply — 'nix flake update' runs as the USER (rewrites flake.lock), then the switch goes through the root helper. The helper deliberately has no lock-update action, so this split is already enforced rather than merely intended.

UI: a tray menu entry. nixadmin-tray is already an SNI applet registered with COSMIC (com.system76.CosmicStatusNotifierWatcher), so no new app is needed. Follow the actions.py pattern: show the diff, get explicit confirmation, then apply.
acceptance_criteria: Tray shows when inputs have moved; applying updates the lock as the user and switches via the confirm-gated helper path. INVARIANT: no auto-apply path that bypasses safety.py — switch/boot must keep requiring explicit confirm after a test. Re-introducing unattended switch would recreate exactly what was deleted.

title: Redact grounding context, tool outputs, and history on escalated queries
description: ADR 0004 v1 redacts only the user's QUERY TEXT before escalation. The remote agent's tools run locally and can pull system state (a failed unit's journal, paths, tokens) into the frontier conversation; system_extra context and history are also sent unredacted. Extend redaction to those payloads so nothing sensitive leaves the device on an escalated query.
notes: 2026-07-26: DONE. _run_remote now deterministically scrubs system_extra (grounding), history, and each tool result on escalated queries; tool dispatch split into _call_tool so scrub lives in one place. Gated to escalated queries by design (remote-default = user opted into cloud). ADR 0004 updated.

title: Tray menu + live updates
description: Menu: status line + failed units, each a Fix-it action -> remediation (which confirms/verifies). Refresh icon+menu from daemon Events and when a unit clears.
close_reason: Per-unit fix-it menu rows (Restart <unit>) via new structured RestartUnit protocol message — deterministic, no NL round-trip; daemon acts only on units it currently reports failed, scope taken from its live view. Live updates via event-driven + post-fix refresh. Factored restart_resolved out of remediation.run.

title: nixadmin-tray: SNI item via dbus-fast
description: Small Python tray client: register a StatusNotifierItem + DBusMenu; status icon green/amber; connect to the daemon socket. Reuses dbus-fast (already a dep). Separate client keeps the daemon headless.
close_reason: SNI tray via dbus-fast: green/amber/grey disc icon, health from daemon ListFailures, DBusMenu status header + Quit, re-registers on host restart. Validated live against cosmic-applet-status-area.

title: Daemon: structured list-failed-units query
description: A protocol query returning failed units as structured data (name, reason, scope system/user) so a client renders per-unit actions, instead of parsing the services fetcher text.
notes: Done on feat/tray. Protocol: ListFailures (client->daemon) + Failures (daemon->client) carrying structured {unit, scope, description} entries. remediation.failed_units() gathers failed .service units across system+user scopes. server._list_failures handles the request. Protocol round-trip tests incl. the list-of-dict field + empty case. nix flake check green.

title: Remediation: route system-unit fix through the helper
description: Extend remediation.py so restarting a failed SYSTEM unit goes via the helper restart action; user units already work. Keep confirm+verify+honest-report.
notes: Done on feat/tray. remediation.run is now scope-aware: gathers system+user units, restarts user units directly and SYSTEM units via injected restart_system (safety.apply_restart -> helper restart action from gav.1); confirm+verify+honest-report preserved, scope-appropriate is-failed/journal-tail. safety: generalized _run_helper to a request dict; added apply_restart(unit). server wires restart_system. Tests: apply_restart protocol (fake helper) + system-scope routing (mocked). nix flake check green. Live end-to-end validation bundled with the backend deploy.

title: Helper: privileged restart <unit> action
description: Add a restart action to nixadmin-helper.py so system units can be restarted via the root helper; validate the unit name; sits alongside the rebuild actions. The one backend gap. Subsumes the generic issue nix-nixadmin-s01.
notes: Code complete on feat/tray: restart action + valid_unit (deny-list + charset/suffix), _run_restart (direct systemctl restart, watchdog), protocol doc. Unit tests for valid_unit; helper flake8 + nix flake check green. Live restart validation bundled with the gav.2 backend deploy (needs a helper-changing switch).

title: PoC: supervised systemd-failure tray
description: First UI increment. An SNI tray item (native to COSMIC status-area via dbus-fast, verified: org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher hosted by cosmic-applet-status-area) that shows overall health and lists failed systemd units in its DBusMenu, each with a Fix-it (restart) action, wired to existing detection (monitors/JobRemoved) + remediation. Supervised mode: human approves each fix; manual precursor to the autofix engine. Inc1=tray+fix (no web). Inc2=Open-detail web view. Design: docs/ux.md. Defers libcosmic-vs-GTK.
close_reason: PoC complete: supervised systemd-failure tray shipped end-to-end. gav.1-8 done and live-validated (deterministic backend, SNI tray with fix-its, autostart, on-demand LLM explain, token-gated web view). gav.9 subsumed by gav.8.

title: Find a better project name + discoverable AI text
description: Rename the project — 'nixadmin' is techy and admin-centric. The name should encode the relationship/trust (see vision.md: 'caring distribution', 'a computer you can give to someone you love'), not the capability. SEPARATELY and intentionally: add AI keywords to the DISCOVERABILITY text (repo description, README, package metadata, topics) so people searching for AI tools can find it — that is how this category is discovered today. The tension is deliberate and resolved by PLACEMENT: 'AI' lives in searchable metadata, NOT in the name or the UI. The product mission stays design-for-silence (ux.md) — AI is an implementation detail, never foregrounded in the experience. Document WHY the AI text exists (findability) so nobody later removes it thinking it violates the no-AI-in-focus principle.

title: Real test harness
description: Fakes for Ollama/LiteLLM/D-Bus + dispatch-branch coverage + golden transcripts. Coverage is smoke-level + 1 integration test today; thin on llm paths, remote tool-loop, monitors, cli, safety socket.

title: Helper returns exit=None on non-helper-changing switch
description: Detached helper returned exit None on a successful switch where the helper did NOT restart (nixlap beads add). Rebuild unit was active-exited. Verify _run_rebuild exit reporting / follower completion when the helper survives.

title: UI toolkit decision: libcosmic vs GTK
description: Native-correct is libcosmic (iced) for the COSMIC lock; GTK fallback. Decide after the interaction model. Notifications+ledger are toolkit-agnostic and shippable first.
notes: Do not introduce a frontend framework during nix-nixadmin-si0. Start with ES modules and explicit state. Reassess Lit only after the extracted UI and overlay spike reveal concrete state-synchronisation pain. Desktop shell decision should include a minimal GTK4/WebKitGTK wrapper alongside native libcosmic/GTK options.

title: Kept-well ledger
description: Looked-after-itself-for-N-days + quiet tally; pull-only, glance-moment (lock screen). Data = audit trail + detectors. docs/ux.md.
notes: 2026-07-26: BUILT. Pure fold nixadmin.ledger.summarize (streak + quiet tally, honest zeroing on live failure), wire get_ledger/ledger (protocol v3), daemon _get_ledger, dclient.ledger(), GET /api/ledger, calm glance line at top of web hub (pull-only, no button). Pure + socket tests. Lock-screen glance-moment surface still deferred (toolkit).

title: Daemon supervision: Restart + watchdog
description: systemd Restart=on-failure + backoff; WatchdogSec/sd_notify so a hung daemon restarts, not just a crashed one.

title: Remediation: offer-after-diagnosis path
description: Want-me-to-restart-it after a diagnosis, then yes. Needs light conversational state.

title: Remediation: restart-loop detection
description: Do not offer a restart systemd already retried and lost (check NRestarts); route to needs-a-real-fix.
notes: 2026-07-26: autofix (e7q) ships a basic restart-loop guard (maxAttempts within a 1h window, from the event store -> inform instead of looping). This issue now covers richer loop detection (rate/burst patterns, cross-reboot) beyond that simple counter.

title: Remediation: session relogin / reboot
description: Offer relogin/reboot for the rebuild_skew/EGL case (graphics broken after a rebuild).

title: Remediation: system units via root helper
description: Restart failed SYSTEM units via the privileged helper. remediation.py is user-units-only today.

title: Desktop notifications + offered fix (2b)
description: org.freedesktop.Notifications with action buttons wired to the Confirm protocol; model-phrased diagnosis on fire. proactive-detectors-plan.md 2b.

title: New-coredump detector
description: Poll coredumpctl; fire on dumps newer than last-seen. Spec: proactive-detectors-plan.md 2a.

title: Process-vanished detector (the 20 percent)
description: Poll liveness for non-unit process exits (the cosmic-panel/dock case; no signal anywhere). Dynamic baseline; fire when a baselined component vanishes. Spec: docs/proactive-detectors-plan.md 2a.

title: Reduce web activity pages to five events
description: The redesigned Activity section is still visually too tall at ten rows. Reduce every timeline page to five events while preserving cursor navigation and the New activity behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The latest Activity view and each older page render at most five events; cursor pagination and New activity behavior remain unchanged; tests and the full flake check pass.
close_reason: Activity pages now show five events; cursor navigation and new-activity behavior are unchanged; full flake check passes.

title: Web url-file is clobbered by a second instance
description:
`_write_url_file` in `src/nixadmin/web/server.py` always writes `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nixadmin-web.url`, ignoring the port it actually bound. `main()`'s `finally` then unlinks that same fixed path.

Two consequences, both hit while developing the single-pane hub (2026-08-13):

* Running a dev instance on `NIXADMIN_WEB_PORT=7688` overwrites the file the real service wrote, so the tray's 'open hub' points at the dev port with the dev token.
* Whichever instance exits first deletes the file for both — the tray then has no URL at all while a healthy server is still listening.

Neither is user-facing on a normal machine (one instance, fixed port), but it makes iterating on the page mildly hazardous and the failure is silent.

Options: include the port in the filename, refuse to start if the file exists and its port is live, or only unlink when the file still names our own port.

title: Escalated changes: preserve technical params through redaction
description: ADR 0004: redacting an escalated open-ended CHANGE can strip values that are part of the request (IPs, paths → [ip], /home/[user]), lowering fidelity of what the frontier receives. Today the remote agent only advises (no file-edit tool) and remote isn't wired, so low stakes. When b4h lands, consider a param-preserving redaction (distinguish third-party PII from request parameters) or an explicit 'send exact wording' opt-in for changes. Surfaced by the code review of feat/invoke-bar.

title: LLM-inferred remediation (propose, never execute)
description: Beyond restart: LLM infers the LIKELY remediation from failure + live state, and flags when a restart WON'T help (config error, disk full) -> steers to the real fix (prevents futile-restart trust erosion). GUARDRAILS (keep translator-never-actor): (1) LLM PROPOSES from a bounded catalog of safe deterministic actions, or proposes a config edit through worktree-validate->confirm->verify->rollback; NEVER emits a command to run (judge over real candidates, like the action tier). (2) Deterministic-first: detect remediation class without the LLM where possible (disk full->df, restart-loop->NRestarts, stuck queue->cups state); LLM judges only the ambiguous residue. (3) Confidence+reversibility gate autonomy: restart=auto/offer; inferred fix=offer-as-hypothesis+confirm; novel=escalate to frontier+change tier. (4) Inference is a hypothesis, verified after acting; never fake confidence.
close_reason: Subsumed by gav.8: the Explain prompt already emits the most-likely fix in plain words (verified live: 'restarting won't fix this — ensure another process isn't using port 631'). A separate propose-never-execute tier would duplicate that. Reopen later if we want structured, clickable guarded suggestions (menu/web rows) rather than prose.

title: LLM-humanized failure explanation (on-demand)
description: First LLM role in the tray: translate raw state -> plain language. Menu label stays DETERMINISTIC (e.g. 'Bluetooth - stopped'; works cold). Detail/Explain invokes the LLM lazily (name-why-fix; reuses the #1 diagnosis pipeline). LLM = translator machine->human, never the actor. Eager-vs-lazy: PoC is lazy (raw until Explain); consider eager-on-failure later since failures are rare.
notes: Decided: LAZY via an explicit 'Explain' button (per failure or overall). Click -> fires the LLM to refine/humanize the raw error; raw stays visible (deterministic, works cold). Reuses the #1 diagnosis pipeline (name-why-fix on the clicked unit) -> mostly wiring. UX: click -> Status('warming up…') -> explanation streams (Delta) over the raw, so the ~6s cold-load feels responsive. Doubles as a prompt-iteration testbed (compare raw vs explained).
close_reason: On-demand ExplainUnit: daemon grounds the local model in the failed unit's journal tail and streams a plain-words what/why/likely-fix; lazy (fires only on click), warms up if cold. Tray adds 'Explain <unit>…' rows that show the answer as a desktop notification (Looking into… bubble updated in place). LLM only translates machine→human — never acts.

title: Open detail -> token-gated localhost web view
description: Open-detail menu item -> xdg-open a 127.0.0.1 page served by a small web sidecar over the daemon socket. Bind 127.0.0.1 only; one-time token in the URL; check Origin/Host (anti DNS-rebinding); request-only (daemon still confirms). Page lists failures + starts the ledger view (nix-nixadmin-9ep).
close_reason: Token-gated loopback web view: a stdlib ThreadingHTTPServer bound to 127.0.0.1, every request gated by an unguessable bearer token + Host + Origin checks (mutations require a matching Origin — request-only, CSRF-safe). Pure protocol client (Daemon over the Unix socket); new UnitJournal/Journal messages for detail. Self-contained HTML page (failures, journal, restart/explain). Tray gains 'Open detail' (xdg-open the token URL). Packaged as nixadmin-web user service (services.nixadmin.web.enable).

title: Package + autostart nixadmin-tray
description: systemd user service in the graphical session; nixlap wiring; icon assets.
close_reason: nixadmin-tray packaged as a console script (already in pyproject) and run from a trayPython env; new services.nixadmin.tray.enable option (default true) provisions a systemd user service bound to graphical-session.target. README updated. nixlap needs no new lines — tray comes on with the daemon.

title: hello.ready remote accuracy

title: Remote chain enablement (proxy / API base)

description: Run nix flake check on push/PR.

title: Machine-profile ContextProvider
description: No built-in machine-profile ContextProvider is registered (interface ready, none supplied). System-prompt assembly has no machine context.

title: Voice as primary invoke
description: Voice invoke for the non-technical user (text = the nerd tool). Flips voice-later ordering.

title: No home of its own vs invoke surface
description: Fold intelligence into native surfaces vs a single light summonable invoke surface. docs/ux.md.
notes: 2026-08-13: DAU feedback — users want one place for admin tasks, installing included; a natural-language way in removes the need for an app 'store' entirely. Web hub rebuilt as a single pane of glass (prompt first + common-action chips + stacked task cards + status). Chips are seeded prompts only, never a second path to the daemon. Spotlight overlay is the intended shape — split out to nix-nixadmin-5rf. See docs/ux.md.

title: Prefetch echoes full multiline command into context
description: prefetch prints the whole cmd string, dumping multiline scripts into model context (noise/dilution). Label by fetcher name instead.

title: Lazy litellm import
description: Keep litellm lazy-imported so the local-only path never loads the heavy remote-surface dep.

title: Helper read timeout in _run_helper
description: Timeout in safety._run_helper so a stuck helper cannot hang the daemon.

title: Version the client-daemon wire protocol
description: Wire protocol has no version in hello (module ABI does); a stale client should fail loud.

title: Self-healing worktrees: prune at startup
description: SIGKILL mid-validation leaks a worktree; run git worktree prune at daemon start.

title: edit_packages property tests
description: hypothesis: add idempotent; add+remove round-trips; remove-absent raises; list delimiters survive.

title: Error-rate spike / OOM / baseline persistence (2c)
description: Deferred fuzzy detectors and persisted baseline. proactive-detectors-plan.md 2c.

title: Event store retention / pruning
description: nixadmin.store (ADR 0003) grows events.db unbounded. Add retention: a periodic DELETE FROM events WHERE ts < now-N, or a max-row cap. Non-urgent on a laptop's event rate; revisit when the DB gets large. recent() already takes a 'since' bound to read a window.

title: History backend (sqlite)
description: History is NullHistory only; SessionState scratch works. Add a persistent backend when needed.
notes: 2026-07-26: persistent SQLite store landed as nixadmin.store (the *system-event timeline*), separate from conversation history. Conversation history.py is still NullHistory — this issue now tracks only that remaining half. See ADR 0003.

title: GitHub-native self-curating issue intake
description: Agent triages GH issues: dedup via embeddings, link duplicates, label, request repro, restate. Embrace AI-authored tickets. docs/ideas.md. Speculative.
